title: Variance Bound for Sign-Valued Functions
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability distribution $\pi$, let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set, and let $B$ be a Fourier basis for real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that is orthonormal for $\pi$ and contains the constant-one function. For $n\ge0$, let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $-1$ and $1$. Every randomized decision tree computing $f$ satisfies that the variance of $f$ under $\pi^n$ is at most twice the sum over coordinates of the probability that the tree queries that coordinate, multiplied by the product influence of that coordinate on $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $B$ is a Fourier basis orthonormal for $\pi$ with a constant-one basis vector
